newsitem.title: MOLDOVA: Moldova urges NATO guarantees for neutral countries.
newsitem.headline: Moldova urges NATO guarantees for neutral countries.

text.p: Moldovan leaders told NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana on Monday that the former Soviet republic was not planning to seek membership in any military bloc but urged the Western alliance to provide security guaranties for countries like it.
"Moldova will not join any military bloc neither now, nor in the future, neither in the West, nor in the East," Foreign Minister Mihai Popov said at a joint news conference with Solana.
Earlier on Monday Moldovan President Petru Luchinschi met Solana, who briefly visited the country on his tour of former Soviet republics which had joined NATO's Partnership for Peace programme.
Luchinschi told Solana that "NATO should provide guarantees for neutral states, which...do not allow stationing foreign troops on their territories," his office said in a statement.
Popov urged NATO, which plans in spite of bitter opposition from Moscow to admit some Eastern European countries as full members, to contribute to political stability and security on the continent .
Moldovan leaders, who vow to keep the country neutral, have expressed worries about neighbouring Romania' intentions to seek NATO membership.
Popov expressed hope that NATO actions would not hurt relations between those states, which want to join NATO, and those which do not.
"We hope that (enlargement) process will encourage Romania to have a basic political treaty with the Republic of Moldova," he said.
Moldova's constitution does not allow the stationing of foreign troops on its territory.

However, 6,000 Russian troops are based in the separatist Dnestr region bordering Ukraine. Separatist leaders declared Dnestr independent in 1990, but no other country has recognised the sliver of industrial land as an independent state.
In 1994, Moldova and Russia signed an agreement to withdraw the troops within three years.
